investigator.method: Level 1 PASSIVE_STATIC (curl, descriptive User-Agent, no authentication/browser) against the venue's official 'Billetterie' page, then Level 2 STRUCTURAL (WordPress REST API route/post-type enumeration) against the same domain. A supplementary, non-escalating check of the third-party ticketing platform (Shotgun.live) the venue's own page embeds was also attempted at Level 1 and returned an explicit bot/rate-limit challenge, honestly recorded as a rejected data_paths candidate rather than a probe_history entry (Rex Club's own official domain, not Shotgun.live, is this investigation's candidate).

probe_history.reason: A plain curl GET of https://rexclub.com/billetterie/ (the site's own 'Programmation' menu item links directly to this same URL — there is no separate programmation page) returned a real WordPress page, but its entire content is a Contact Form 7 form ('Formulaire de contact') plus a client-rendered <iframe data-lazy-src="https://shotgun.live/fr/venues/rex-club?noBack=true&embedded=true"> placeholder. No dated event data, JSON-LD, ICS link, or calendar markup of any kind is present in the static response. The homepage (https://rexclub.com/) was also fetched and confirms genuine venue identity but carries no event listing either.

Enumerated this WordPress site's own REST API (wp-json root: registered namespaces oembed/aiarc/akismet/contact-form-7/loginpress/rankmath/complianz/wp-rocket/google-site-kit/aios/mcp/wp-v2/wp-site-health/wp-block-editor/wp-abilities — no calendar/events/Tribe namespace) and its registered post types (wp/v2/types: post, page, attachment, nav_menu_item, wp_block, wp_template*, wp_global_styles, wp_navigation, wp_font_family, wp_font_face, resident, rm_content_editor). The one non-standard type, 'resident', was sampled directly and confirmed to hold DJ-residency bio pages (e.g. 'GREG' / 'GREG RESIDENCY'), not dated events. No queryable events/calendar route exists anywhere on this domain.

blockers.description: Rex Club's own official domain (rexclub.com) exposes no independently-parseable event data at Level 1 or Level 2 — its programme lives entirely on a third-party platform, Shotgun.live, embedded only as a client-rendered iframe widget. Shotgun.live itself, probed directly and honestly at Level 1 (a single plain GET, no bypass attempted), returned an explicit HTTP 429 'Vercel Security Checkpoint' response carrying an 'X-Vercel-Mitigated: challenge' header — a genuine, explicit access control this policy prohibits attempting to defeat (see docs/SOURCE_INVESTIGATION_POLICY.md's 'What may AI NOT infer?': never defeat a CAPTCHA/challenge or bypass explicit access controls). No stable public JSON/API path for Shotgun could be confirmed as a result; per this task's brief this was the one alternative path worth checking, and it is genuinely BLOCKED, not merely unexplored.

Even setting the Shotgun.live challenge aside, actually acquiring this venue's programme would require a client-side-rendered widget to be observed via browser/headless automation (Level 3+) — explicitly out of scope for this investigation per its brief ('Only Level 1 (PASSIVE_STATIC) and Level 2 (STRUCTURAL) — no browser automation').

reasons: Level 1 (rexclub.com's own 'Billetterie'/'Programmation' page): INSUFFICIENT — a contact form plus a client-rendered third-party iframe, no dated events, no JSON-LD/ICS/calendar markup.
Level 2 (rexclub.com's own WordPress REST API): INSUFFICIENT — no calendar/events namespace or post type exists; the one non-standard post type ('resident') is DJ bios, not events.

The one credible alternative path this task's brief specifically asked to check — Shotgun.live, the third-party platform Rex Club's own site embeds — returned an explicit, header-confirmed bot/rate-limit challenge (HTTP 429, X-Vercel-Mitigated: challenge) when probed honestly at Level 1. This is a genuine BLOCKED finding, not an unexplored option; per policy, BLOCKED terminates escalation and must never be bypassed.

No usable public acquisition path was found for this candidate within the levels this investigation is authorised to use. DEFER is the honest, policy-correct outcome — not every investigation must reach activation, and this one genuinely cannot without either defeating an explicit access control or introducing browser automation, both out of scope here.
